root_cause.text: The IRC conntrack helper’s command-scanning loop in `nf_conntrack_irc.c:help()` continued checking other commands after `parse_dcc()` had already matched a DCC command but failed to parse its arguments, leaving parsing state at an invalid position and causing a possible out-of-bounds read.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes both failure paths after a matched DCC command from `continue;` to `goto out;`, and the commit/CVE explicitly state: “When parsing fails after we've matched the command string we should bail out instead of trying to match a different command,” fixing a “possible out-of-bounds read.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix parse failure handling by exiting through the function's common out path instead of continuing processing after an unparseable DCC command.
intent_record.what: The change replaces a `continue;` statement with `goto out;` inside the branch that handles a failed `parse_dcc(...)` call after logging "unable to parse dcc command".
intent_record.how: At runtime, when DCC command parsing fails, execution now exits through the function's `out` path instead of skipping to the next loop iteration. This changes error handling flow so the function stops normal per-iteration processing and follows its common exit/cleanup path, preventing further processing after a parse failure.

intent_record.intent_summary: Abort processing on forged DCC commands by exiting the helper early instead of continuing the loop.
intent_record.what: The control flow in the forged DCC command handling path was changed from `continue;` to `goto out;` after logging a ratelimited warning when the parsed DCC IP/port is considered forged.
intent_record.how: Instead of skipping only the current iteration and continuing further processing, the function now exits through the `out` label immediately when a forged DCC command is detected, preventing any subsequent parsing or expectation setup in that call.

consistency_review.core_intent: Stop further processing of invalid or forged DCC commands by exiting the helper early through the function's shared exit path.

After finding "\1DCC ", the code enters `for (i = 0; i < ARRAY_SIZE(dccprotos); i++)` and, on a protocol match, does `data += strlen(dccprotos[i]);` before calling `parse_dcc(...)`. If `parse_dcc(...)` fails, it executes `continue;` (`if (parse_dcc(...) ) { DEBUGP("unable to parse dcc command\n"); continue; }`). This means the loop continues checking other DCC commands even though `data` has already been advanced past the matched command token, leaving parsing state changed/invalid for subsequent iterations. That matches the root cause exactly: continued scanning after `parse_dcc()` matched a DCC command but failed to parse arguments. There is no protective handling such as breaking out, resetting `data`, or aborting processing on parse failure, so the fix is not present.
